description: Provider failover inside one request: which upstream calls happen, what the client gets, Retry-After forwarding, and billing of the successful attempt only. Cases use openai/gpt-oss-120b on DeepInfra, Together and Groq with provider.order pinned.

entries.description: A failed first attempt moves to the next eligible provider, which serves and is the only one billed.

source.note: Fallback behavior: if a provider returns errors or rate limits, the Gateway can retry or route to another provider that supports the same model.
Fallback flowchart: provider error -> another eligible provider -> success -> return the response.

source.reason: A failed provider attempt returned no output and no usage, so only the attempt that served the response is billable; the docs bill each served attempt exactly as without fallbacks.

source.note: usage.prompt_tokens / completion_tokens of the serving provider (Together, OpenAI-compatible) priced with its catalogue card.
Phaseo forwards a validated Retry-After value when the routed provider supplies one; the provider that served the response sent none.

source.reason: The 300 ms GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS deadline elapsed on the first provider; the attempt log should name the timeout so request logs explain the failover.

source.note: Every eligible provider is tried before the error is returned.
Example error response for a provider failure.
failed_providers, failed_statuses, and attempt_count: extra retry and failover context.

source.reason: No provider produced output or usage, so nothing is billable; failed requests are never charged to the wallet.

source.note: 500-599: Phaseo or upstream provider failure; example upstream_error with status_code 502.
Phaseo forwards a validated Retry-After value when the routed provider supplies one.

source.reason: Mixed 5xx and 429 failures: either the throttling status (limits.mdx: a request can still return 429) or the generic upstream 502 is acceptable.

entries.description: Once the upstream stream has started producing output there is no failover and no double billing.

source.note: Streaming: fallbacks happen only before the first byte is sent. An error after a stream has started is returned in that stream.

source.reason: One upstream generation can be charged at most once, whatever happened to the stream.

source.note: An error after a stream has started is returned in that stream.
If it fails mid-stream, treat the partial stream as incomplete: no successful terminal frame may follow.
Streaming-specific notes: if the request fails before streaming begins (to the client), you get a standard JSON error payload. A buffered client received no bytes before the upstream failed.

source.reason: An upstream stream that ended in an error is not a successful request and must not be logged as one.
